mechanism.claim: A fresh crossing into an extreme imbalance between positive and negative five-minute realized semivariance during high six-hour realized volatility marks one-sided short-horizon displacement that should partially reverse.
mechanism.side: fade the dominant semivariance: positive dominance short, negative dominance long
mechanism.why_distinct: HVSIR uses an irregular five-minute threshold-crossing clock and signed squared-return mass. It is not HVSER's six-hour anchor/sign entropy continuation, JVFCR's jump-flow continuation, or any terminal rule/control modification.
mechanism.why_low_gross9_overlap_is_plausible: entries occur only on first 5m crossings of a source-calibrated semivariance tail, rather than on scheduled clocks or existing Gross9 feature conditions

clock.positive_semivariance: sum squared positive returns over trailing 72 bars
clock.negative_semivariance: sum squared negative returns over trailing 72 bars
clock.calibration: 2023H1 source-only anchors freeze absolute imbalance q80 and realized-volatility q70; no forward return, execution price, funding PnL, or Gross9 row is opened
clock.trigger: current abs imbalance >= frozen q80, immediately prior completed bar abs imbalance < q80, current realized volatility >= frozen q70
clock.reservation: global half-open; exit first on equal open

economic_gates.accounting: fixed quantity, exact funding marks, 6bp base and 10bp stress per notional side, every held 5m favorable then adverse, global HWM, full-calendar CAGR

source_plan.execution_prices: sealed until source support and Gross9 novelty both pass

stopping_rule: freeze preregistration, open source incidence, then Gross9 novelty and sequential economics; terminal first frozen failure with no threshold, hold, side, or clock repair
